author: landseerenga
text:
every App Store rejection costs you 2-5 days.

so we built a cli that scans your iOS app against apple's guidelines before you submit.

> payment & IAP compliance
> privacy manifests & data declarations
> required sign-in & account deletion flows
> metadata & completeness checks
> binary validation

now with a added cloud device feature, so it validates full user flows, not just the binary.

made it a claude code and codex skill. it fixes every issue it finds. scan, fix, repeat until it passes.

author: wesroth
text:
Cursor released its native iOS app.

Developers can now launch always-on cloud agents from their phones or remotely control agents running on their computers.

The app supports:

🔹Voice instructions and slash commands
🔹Live Activities on the lock screen
🔹Notifications when an agent finishes or needs input
🔹Reviews of demos, screenshots, logs and code changes
🔹Follow-up instructions
🔹Pull-request merging
🔹Handoffs between local and cloud agents

Cloud agents run inside isolated development environments where they can edit code, run tests and continue working without keeping the phone app open.

Cursor for iOS is available in public beta on all paid plans.

author: uzairansar
text:
I was on the subway in NYC, talking to my Hermes agent thru Telegram.

Loved Hermes. Telegram, not so much. How sick would it be to interface with my agent through something as sleek as the ChatGPT app.

So I started looking for an iOS app for this. There wasn't one.

I run my own agent because it's mine: server, data, rules, etc. and because it can actually do real things

So I decided to build the the app myself.

I'd never built an iOS app, and I don't really know Swift. The last app I tried to make was a calculator, when I was 15. But I wanted this one enough that I used AI to figure the whole thing out - building an AI client with AI. Big brain move.

That app is Hermex.

It feels like the ChatGPT app, except it's pointed at my own Hermes agent. And now I reach for Hermex over the ChatGPT app for most things.

Still early, but if that sounds like your kind of thing, check it out 👇

author: vaibhavsisinty
text:
OpenClaw just launched on iOS and Android.

Your phone is not the assistant.

It is a node.

The actual agent runs on a Gateway you control. Not a company server. Not someone else's cloud.

You decide what it sees.

Camera, location, contacts, calendar. All optional. All approved by you.
Bring your own API key. Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, whatever you choose.

Here is the part that matters.

Apple used to block agentic AI from the App Store entirely. Too much device access. Too much trust required.

This approval just broke that wall.

A self hosted, open source AI agent is now sitting right next to ChatGPT
and Gemini.

That is not a small thing.

author: ewtnews
text:
For many Catholics, faith formation often competes with busy schedules and endless digital distractions. Fio, a Catholic audio streaming platform, hopes to change that by putting faith-filled content at listeners’ fingertips.

Dubbed “the Catholic alternative to Spotify,” the platform offers a growing library of podcasts, audiobooks, and music, giving users a way to stay connected to their faith wherever life takes them.

Currently, Fio is being used in over 100 countries, is host to over 100,000 hours of Catholic content, and has over 1,000 Catholic creators putting their work onto the platform.

Will Hickl, co-founder of Fio, has been in the music industry for 15 years as a musician and founder of the Catholic record label NOVUM RECORDS. During his career, he realized that secular platforms were not built for faith-based work — it was difficult to stand out, there was no fair compensation, and there was no community around it.

With this in mind, Hickl, and co-founder Peter Buonincontro, launched Fio in 2023. The first version of the app hosted podcasts alone. The following year music was added, and the following year — thanks to a generous investor — the platform was able to host audiobooks and grow their collection of content. 

In an interview with EWTN News, Hickl shared that the platform’s “North Star” is the fact that he cares deeply about the artists and content creators.

“We are a platform who, because we care, weʼre paying a penny per stream, which is already three to four times what Spotify pays,” he explained. “We want to offer better exposure and tooling. In fact, we already offer better exposure because a musician doesnʼt have to compete with 10 million other musicians. Thereʼs only maybe like 100, maybe 200 artists on the platform right now…thereʼs greater discoverability.”

For creators, he hopes they would know that Fio “is the one that genuinely cares about them more than Apple or Spotify ever will.”

Currently, Fio offers three subscription levels for listeners — free, premium, and audiobooks +. While users who subscribe to the platform for free will have to listen to advertisements, Hickl pointed out that these ads “are reserved and curated for Catholic businesses, Catholic ministries, and then Catholic artists on the platform.”

He also emphasized that these faith-based advertisements can also serve as a “cultural safeguard” so that parents who may be listening with children present don’t have to worry about inappropriate advertisements being played, as is the case with many secular platforms.

Hickl explained that Fio aims to serve three different cohorts: Catholic creators, consumers, and businesses.

“We are an artist first platform. We want to give you the best exposure, the best economics than any other platform,” he said. “For consumers, we want to give you greater choice, a better experience in terms of what you find, what your kids are exposed to. The third would be Catholic businesses who canʼt target based on religion on Facebook or Google or YouTube or anything like that. So weʼre offering a greater targeting mechanism, greater value in that regard.”

For those seeking to have their content on Fio, they must go through a submission and review process. Before their content is accepted, creators must affirm that they are practicing Catholics who accept the teachings of the Church. They must also verify that their work was not primarily created by artificial intelligence. Lastly, each creator goes through a manual review process by the Fio team before their work is allowed to be on the platform.

Looking to the future, the team at Fio is working on creating original content for the platform as well as being able to host video podcasts and music videos. Additionally, they are working to give Fio a more “liturgical feel.” For example, if there’s an important saint’s feast day, Fio would make suggestions to listeners of a podcast that talks about the saint or a song inspired by the saint.

Hickl hopes that one day more artists will “be more excited about sharing their Fio link than the Spotify link.”

He added that he hopes Catholics “would know I can trust this platform, it can and should be a part of my every day, because thereʼs so much treasure to discover.”

“Thatʼs something I say a lot, which is that the Church has an immense amount of treasure and we just donʼt know about it. And so I want people to know the treasure is here and Fio is a place where itʼs aggregated,” he said.

Fio can be downloaded on iOS, Android, and streamed through your web browser.

https://t.co/4yjEEibdc0

author: snskritinaruka
text:
OpenClaw is now available on both iOS and Android.

What’s interesting is that your phone isn’t the AI assistant itself, it’s simply the interface.

The real AI agent runs on a Gateway that you host and control, not on a company’s servers or a third-party cloud.

You choose exactly what it can access.

Camera, location, contacts, calendar every permission is optional and granted only if you allow it.

You also bring your own model and API key, whether that’s Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or another provider.

But the biggest story isn’t the app itself.

Until recently, Apple was reluctant to allow highly agentic AI apps on the App Store because of the level of device access and user trust they require.

OpenClaw’s approval signals that this is beginning to change.

For the first time, a self-hosted, open-source AI agent can sit alongside apps like ChatGPT and Gemini on the App Store.

That’s a much bigger milestone than it might seem at first glance.

Cursor just shipped a native iOS app. Public beta.

What's in it:

> Launch cloud agents from your phone (they run in isolated VMs, your laptop stays closed)
> Remote-control desktop agents while you're away from your computer
> Voice input and slash commands to brief them
> Live Activities and push notifications when work is ready for review
> Merge PRs directly from the app

Composer 2.5 is 75% off in the app through July 5.

The shift nobody's framing: developers were the last knowledge workers tethered to a laptop. Cursor just made the LAPTOP optional. Coding is becoming an "agent supervision from anywhere" job, not a "keyboard at desk" job.

Slack did this for office workers in 2014. It took 10 years to reach engineering.

Clip below.

text:
Cursor just shipped a mobile app — and it changes how I think about AI code editors.

Cursor for iOS/Mac lets you build apps by describing them in natural language on your phone. The AI generates the code, previews it, and you can iterate in real-time.

It's not "write code on your phone" (nobody wants that). It's "concept → prototype in seconds" wherever you are.

You describe a feature while commuting, refine it, then open it on desktop fully formed. The gap between idea and implementation just got narrower.

This is the UX direction every AI coding tool should study.

Available now on the App Store.

author: pierreanalyzes
text:
POV: The AI race is quietly shifting from models to operating systems.

This week alone:

• OpenAI is making Codex faster and easier to direct.
• Cursor launched an iPhone app to manage always-on coding agents.
• OpenClaw is pushing developers toward the same future.

Most people will see three product launches.

I see the early blueprint of a new computing model.

For decades, software has been something you used.

Open an app.
Click a button.
Complete a task.
Close the app.

AI changes that.

Instead of using software, you’ll increasingly delegate work to software.

Your role shifts from operator to manager.

That’s a fundamental change in how humans interact with computers.

And it has consequences far beyond coding.

• The winning products won’t just have the best models—they’ll have the best workflows.
• The most valuable interfaces won’t be the ones you use the most, but the ones you barely notice because they’re working continuously.
• Competitive advantage will come from orchestration, memory, context, and trust—not raw intelligence alone.

I think we’re entering the era of AI operating systems, where the product isn’t the chatbot.

The product is an intelligent workforce that quietly gets things done while you focus on higher-value decisions.

If that happens, we’ll look back at “opening an app” the same way we now look at manually saving files: a habit from an earlier era.

author: tekscreate
text:
Blitz — automates App Store Connect submissions and IAP management from your terminal.

Every iOS developer knows the pain: uploading screenshots, filling metadata, updating in-app purchases, submitting for review. Apple's App Store Connect interface is functional but manual. Blitz wraps it all in a CLI.

What it handles:

- App metadata updates (name, description, keywords, promo text)
- Screenshot uploads across all device frames and languages
- IAP product creation and management
- App version creation and submission flow
- Promo code generation and redemption tracking

Open source, Mac-native, works with CI/CD pipelines. If you manage more than one app, this pays for itself on the first submission.

The indie dev and small studio market is underserved for App Store tooling. Fastlane has been the default for years, but it's aging — Ruby dependencies, fragile configuration, slow to update for new App Store Connect API changes. Blitz is built on the newer ASC API v3 and written in Swift.

Worth watching: if Apple doesn't ship better first-party CLI tooling for App Store Connect, tools like Blitz will become essential infrastructure for anyone shipping on iOS.

https://t.co/2yUl9fEONX
